root_cause.text: The `container_of` macro was used on a `file` pointer that was not guaranteed to be a member of a `linux_binprm` structure, causing invalid pointer arithmetic and a stack-out-of-bounds read when the pointer pointed to a stack-local variable instead.
root_cause.evidence: The KASAN report shows a stack-out-of-bounds read in `ima_appraise_measurement` triggered by the `is_bprm_creds_for_exec` function, which used `container_of(&file, struct linux_binprm, file)` to compute a `bprm` pointer. The patch removes this dangerous container_of usage and instead passes a `bprm_is_check` boolean directly from the caller (`ima_bprm_check`), which has legitimate access to the `bprm->is_check` field.
